title: Universal injectivity descends for finitely presented qcqs models
statement: Let D be a directed inverse system with affine transition maps and limit c, and p:Y→D_i a finitely presented qcqs morphism over a qcqs stage. If its base change to c is universally injective, its base change to a later stage D_j is universally injective. proof.text: Universal injectivity means surjectivity of the diagonal. The diagonal of p is locally finitely presented and its source and target are qcqs. The diagonal base-change isomorphism gives a surjective diagonal at the limit. Apply surjectivity descent to the diagonal as a morphism over D_i. Reinsert the diagonal base-change isomorphism at that stage and apply the criterion. Pullback symmetry gives the second-projection presentation.

theorem exists_universallyInjective_pullback_stage
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i : I)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj (op i))] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj (op i))]
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ D.obj (op i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    (hp : UniversallyInjective (pullback.snd p (c.π.app (op i)))) :
    ∃ (j : I) (h : i ≤ j),
      UniversallyInjective (pullback.snd p (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
